sentences.text: Gnathosaurus is a genus of ctenochasmatid pterosaur that includes two species, G. subulatus and G. macrurus.
The skull of G. subulatus was slender, measuring 28 cm in length, and featured up to 130 needle-like teeth arranged along a spoon-shaped tip.
This animal belongs to the family Ctenochasmatidae and is classified within the subfamily Gnathosaurinae.
It is conjectured that Gnathosaurus used its teeth to filter water and capture small animals.
Gnathosaurus jaw fragments were first found in 1832 in southern Germany but were initially misidentified as a crocodile jaw and named Crocodilus multidens.
A more complete adult skull was discovered in 1951 and classified as Gnathosaurus subulatus.
A large specimen originally named Pterodactylus macrurus was found in the Purbeck Limestone of England.
Scientists like Albert Oppel concluded that Gnathosaurus was a flying reptile rather than a crocodilian.
Gnathosaurus fossils date back to the Late Jurassic period.
Gnathosaurus lived between 168.2 and 137.05 million years ago, from the Bathonian to the Berriasian stages.
Bennett (2025) concluded that Aurorazhdarcho micronyx is a junior synonym of Gnathosaurus subulatus based on comparisons with juvenile specimens.
